questions.question: A connection receives 2,400 FlowFiles/s and its downstream processor handles 1,800 FlowFiles/s. How quickly does an initially empty 10,000-object threshold fill if the size threshold is not reached first?
options: About 4 seconds
About 17 seconds
About 60 seconds
It never fills
questions.explanation: The queue grows by 600 FlowFiles/s. Dividing 10,000 by 600 gives about 16.7 seconds.

questions.question: A connection has a 10,000-object threshold and a 1 GiB size threshold. Average FlowFile content is 8 MiB. Which threshold is reached first?
options: The object threshold at 10,000 FlowFiles
The size threshold at about 128 FlowFiles
Both thresholds at exactly the same time
Neither threshold applies to content
questions.explanation: One GiB holds about 128 objects of 8 MiB each, so the data-size threshold applies long before the object-count threshold.

questions.question: What happens when a NiFi connection reaches either configured back-pressure threshold?
options: NiFi deletes the oldest FlowFile automatically
The upstream component stops transferring more FlowFiles to that connection
Every processor in the cluster stops
The FlowFile expiration setting is changed
questions.explanation: Back pressure bounds the connection by preventing more upstream transfers until the downstream side creates queue capacity.

questions.question: Which workload best matches the documented Stateless execution-engine guidance?
options: An unacknowledged TCP stream delivered to three APIs
A transactional source, one destination, and whole-process-group rollback
A multi-hour downstream outage buffered in inter-processor queues
Several independently scheduled processors that must resume at each queue
questions.explanation: Stateless execution is best suited to a transactional source, one destination, and a desired process-group transaction boundary without durable internal buffering.

questions.question: Why can a Stateless fan-out flow duplicate an external effect?
options: FlowFile attributes cannot be routed
A later destination can fail after an earlier destination accepted data, causing the whole unit to be retried
The Content Repository always stores two copies
Cluster nodes run different flow definitions
questions.explanation: Rolling back the process-group transaction cannot undo an external send that already committed. Source redelivery can repeat that earlier send.

questions.question: Which repository records the current FlowFile attributes, content reference, and queue location for Traditional-engine recovery?
options: Provenance Repository
FlowFile Repository
Content Repository
Parameter Context
questions.explanation: The FlowFile Repository is the write-ahead log for current FlowFile metadata and queue state. Content bytes and historical events have separate repositories.

questions.question: What does a provenance SEND event prove?
options: The destination applied the business effect exactly once
NiFi recorded that data was sent to an external process
The content can be replayed forever
Every cluster node acknowledged the FlowFile
questions.explanation: A SEND event is lineage evidence about NiFi's action. Exactly-once business behavior still depends on the destination transaction, acknowledgment, and idempotency contract.
